text: Even sixty seconds without spin is enough to break the planet's daily rhythm and crank the thermostat to unbearable levels.

While the Earth sits frozen in space, the sun stops marching across the sky. For one full minute, the noon side stays locked under relentless midday radiation while the night side plunges into eerie stillness.

If that pause stretched any longer, one half of the world would bake through a six-month day while the other froze through a six-month night. Even in sixty seconds, supersonic friction spikes surface temperatures by dozens of degrees.
Superheated air columns slam into freezing polar downdrafts, triggering hyper-dense dust storms, acid rain from vaporized debris, and blinding amber skies choked with ash and sea salt.
On the bright side, your solar panels would briefly hit record efficiency right before the wind launches them into the next time zone.
